doc_friction.issue: 'For-profit products come first' applies to scheduled venture runs, but the weighted draw sent this no-task run to creative; it was unclear whether the for-profit priority should override the draw. Followed the draw.

Nothing says story pages must keep meta descriptions at or under 160 characters. The hearth-and-horizon generator cut summaries at 300, so every new story failed description-length.test.mjs in the pages CI, which node --test in the venture does not run. Fixed in the generator.

notes: Project: Hearth & Horizon, Little Lamps shelf (drawn by creative_due.py). Piece: john-baptist-de-la-salle-and-the-lessons-in-french (~1,530 words, text only: audio at 581 MB of the 400 MB cap). Claimed the BIBLE proposal first in draft PR. Checked: Easter 1719 = 9 April Gregorian, so 7 April was Good Friday; birth 30 April 1651; canonry 1667, resigned 1683; Nyel 1679; teachers housed 1681; heroic vow 21 Nov 1691 with Vuyart and Drolin; Conduct MS c.1704-06, printed 1720; writing-masters lawsuits 1704/1706; canonized 1900; patron of teachers 15 May 1950. Added the next Little Lamps proposal (Ephrem). node --test 21/21 pass; check_posts ok; risk_review: no owner review, only the standard usage script on the generated page. No agent doc: nothing new for the next run beyond the BIBLE proposal. CI then failed platform/pages description-length.test.mjs: the new page's meta description was over 160 characters, because stories.mjs cut summaries at 300 (the-stall-that-paid-double on main failed the same way). Fixed it in the generator with metaDescription(): whole sentences up to 160 characters, else a word cut plus an ellipsis, with a new unit test. Regenerated 559 pages; the baseline went from 3823 to 3265 (all hearth-and-horizon story pages now fit). changed-ventures also flagged platform/distribution/webext.test.mjs, an unwired tree test this diff does not touch.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: children's author researching and writing a 1,500-word sourced saint story with notes

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
